A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TorchTitan. Their main text, figures, tables, code listings and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: Section 3 reports original Llama 3.1 training-throughput and memory experiments on H100 GPUs, including comparisons of compilation, Float8, AsyncTP and pipeline schedules.

after.justification: v3 retains the original performance experiments and adds long-context training results in Tables 5–6 and loss-convergence experiments in Appendix B.10.

M1.justification: Context parallelism and zero-bubble schedules move from ongoing work in v1 Section 4.1 to implemented capabilities. v3 adds composable 4D training through sequence sharding, attention-operator replacement and DTensor extensions, plus ZeroBubble and Flexible-Interleaved-1F1B scheduling support.

E1.justification: The C4 English corpus and Llama model family are retained, but Tables 5–6 add explicit long-context training scenarios spanning 32,768–262,144 tokens for 8B and 405B models. These substantially extend the evaluated input conditions beyond v1's reported scenarios.

E2.justification: v3 adds direct feature comparisons against Megatron-LM, DeepSpeed and veScale in Table 7, and code-size comparisons against Megatron-LM and DeepSpeed in Table 8. These expand comparative evaluation beyond v1's internal optimization comparisons, although they are not competing-system throughput benchmarks.

E3.justification: New experiments sweep CP degrees 1, 2, 4 and 8 alongside context length, and compare loss across parallelism configurations over 3,000 steps with 600 warmup steps and fixed global batch size 32. The original throughput-sampling procedure and Tables 1–4 configuration descriptions remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B.10 adds correctness checks comparing loss trajectories for FSDP, FSDP+CP, 3D and 4D configurations (Figure 5, Table 9). Tables 5–6 additionally examine context-length scaling with CP degree. These substantially extend v1's throughput-oriented optimization ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed evaluations, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Figure 5's multiple curves represent different configurations, not repeated runs or uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v3 adds CP throughput/memory results, convergence curves and code-size measurements. Table 2 revises the compiler-only row from 7,168 tokens/sec, +26.97% and 62.0 GiB to 6,482, +14.82% and 62.1 GiB. The headline optimized speedups remain unchanged, while v1 Appendix B.2's observed 3–6x HSDP scaling extension is removed.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theorems, proofs or mathematical derivations. The added CP material describes implementation and empirical behavior without introducing formal mathematical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion expand the central capability claim from composable 3D training to implemented 4D parallelism enabling long-context training. The PyTorch-native unification claim and original headline speedups are retained.

C2.justification: v3 adds guidance on CP placement within the device mesh and explains using ZeRO-2 with PP to avoid repeated parameter all-gathers. Appendix B.10 also explicitly assumes FSDP correctness when interpreting the new convergence checks. Most existing scaling interpretations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds CP context-manager code, and Appendix B.10 newly specifies ZeRO-3 outside PP, ZeRO-2 with PP, and convergence-test budgets. The ZeRO-stage statement is additional disclosure, not evidence that retained experiments were rerun. Hardware, tokenizer and repository access information remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: The broad related-work paragraph becomes detailed positioning against Megatron-LM, DeepSpeed and veScale, supplemented by feature and code-complexity comparisons in Appendix B.9. Slapo and additional scheduling work are introduced, while the NeMo and torchtune discussion is removed.

P1.justification: Substantial rewriting and compression affect the introduction, initialization and pipeline explanations, debugging discussion, scaling guidance and conclusion. The standalone adaptability section is removed, with implemented capabilities integrated into the method, scaling discussion and expanded appendices.

P2.justification: v3 redraws Figures 1–2 to incorporate additional capabilities and 4D scaling, adds Tables 5–9 and the convergence plot in Figure 5, and relocates the unchanged Figures 3–4. Existing performance-table captions also explicitly identify per-GPU statistics.

improvement.justification: v3 supplies convergence evidence missing from v1's correctness claims and turns planned context parallelism into documented, experimentally demonstrated long-context and 4D training. These additions substantially strengthen validation of the system's central composability claim, while new implementation disclosures improve reproducibility. External-system comparisons remain limited to features and code size, and run-to-run uncertainty is still unreported.
